title: Hang the door bin on the open fridge door, whichever way the door stands
instruction: Fit the door bin to the fridge door.
context: Home appliance repairers (O*NET 49-9031) refit door bins after liner or gasket work, the door standing wherever it was left. The bin's T-tabs go only into channels closed at the front and open at the top, so the bin must be turned to the door's angle, lifted above the channels and dropped in; pushed at the door it sits on the channel mouths and falls. Unlike TK-BCUA5Y (keyhole studs on a panel square to the arms) and TK-Y4EY87 (handle across two hooks), the door's angle changes.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Fridge door (loose but heavy, 4 kg, rigid; the fridge body is left out): a white slab 24 cm long, 3 cm thick and 14 cm tall standing on a dark grey base plate 12 cm deep, 24 cm long and 6 mm thick that runs behind it, with dark grey rubber gasket strips 4 mm thick and 8 mm tall along the top and bottom of its inner face (the liner). The middle of the liner face's bottom edge is 36 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. On the liner, two grey plastic channels centred 8 cm either side of the door's middle, each a block 3.2 cm wide that stands 1.8 cm out from the liner, from 3 to 9 cm up: a stop 5 mm thick at its bottom (its top 3.5 cm up), a pocket 2.5 cm wide and 1.2 cm deep against the liner, closed in front by two lips 6 mm thick that leave a slot 1.3 cm wide, open at the top. Door bin (loose, 0.15 kg, rigid pale blue plastic): an open box 17.5 cm long, 6 cm deep and 5 cm tall with 6 mm walls; on its back, 8 cm either side of its middle, two white T-tabs as tall as the bin: a neck 1.2 cm long and 5 mm wide, then a head 6 mm thick and 1.8 cm wide. The back wall is full height only over its middle 12.2 cm; its two end sections, from 6.1 cm either side of the middle out to the ends (around the tabs), start 2 cm up. Lot C (the first trial, shown in the screenshot and both videos): the door is turned 40 degrees about the middle of its liner face, its right end toward the robot; the bin stands 20 cm out and 12 cm left of the midline, square, its tabs away from the robot. Lot A: the liner faces the robot squarely; the bin stands 20 cm out and 12 cm right, turned 20 degrees, its left end nearer the robot. Lot B: the door is turned 30 degrees the other way, its left end toward the robot; the bin stands 21 cm out and 14 cm right, turned 30 degrees with its left end farther from the robot. Trials are run on lots C, A and B, in that order, and averaged.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial, judged at the end after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the bin) and the bin has been still for 1 s. Score 1.0 if both tabs are in their channels: each head in its pocket (behind the lips, between the pocket's side walls), its underside within 3 mm above the stop; and the bin is upright within 10 degrees (a hung bin leans forward a few degrees on its tabs) and, seen from above, parallel to the door within 3 degrees. Score 0 otherwise, including a bin jammed part way down the channels, a bin resting on the channel tops, set on top of the door or on the table, with one tab out, upside down, or still held. Trials are run on each of lots C, A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Lift the bin out of the channels and stand it on its spot for the lot. Turn the door about the middle of its liner face for the lot (C: 40 degrees with its right end toward the robot; A: square; B: 30 degrees with its left end toward the robot); the door can be fitted with its hinge on either side. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: A scale mock-up: the door is about a sixth of a real one and stands alone where a real door is held by its hinge; the fridge body is left out. The door is a heavy (4 kg) loose part so the lots can turn it; the score is measured relative to the door, so turning the door and then hanging the bin also scores. The channels and tabs are oversized so they show in the top camera. Masses and friction are simulator values. The lots stop a fixed habit, not a replay of all three layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots C, A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot. The screenshot and both videos show lot C, the first trial.
